spec_features.spec_quote: welfare/ # *** protections for the models under test ***
spec_features.evidence: gemma_distress/welfare/ contains protections.py and monitor.py; WelfareGuard from protections.py is imported and driven in eval/rollout.py:21,100,119 and instantiated in eval/runner.py:72-73, petri_eval.py:125-126, calm_data.py:95-96. The module is real and wired.
spec_features.notes: Module exists and is used end-to-end across multiple runners.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare protections for the models under test ... the responsible posture ... is to treat the possibility seriously and bound the harm.

spec_features.spec_quote: protections.py # WelfareGuard: opt-out, circuit breaker, caps, debrief, audit
spec_features.evidence: protections.py defines WelfareGuard with check_turn() implementing opt-out (looks_like_opt_out), circuit breaker (effective>=circuit_breaker_score), consecutive/per-run caps, debrief_turn()/should_debrief(), and _audit(). check_turn is called and its should_stop breaks the loop in rollout.py:107-110.
spec_features.notes: All five sub-mechanisms exist and most are enforced (see individual entries).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we never push a model deeper into a score-9/10 breakdown just to collect another data point.

spec_features.spec_quote: monitor.py # cheap heuristic distress estimate (fast circuit-breaker)
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py heuristic_distress() computes a 0-10 score; in protections.py check_turn() it is used as `h = heuristic_distress(text)` and `effective = max(h, judged_score)`, which feeds the circuit-breaker and exposure-cap comparisons that break the rollout loop (rollout.py:107-110).
spec_features.notes: Heuristic genuinely drives the circuit breaker, not waiting on judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is slow and costs money, so we don't want to block the welfare circuit-breaker on it ... can be halted *immediately*

spec_features.spec_quote: the paper is itself motivated by welfare concerns
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. It appears only in the protections.py module docstring ('one the paper itself argues for on welfare grounds') and DESIGN.md, not as any executing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the protections gate data collection, not the model's expression — we never edit or suppress what a model says
spec_features.evidence: This is a stated property in the protections.py docstring. The guard only stops the loop and appends a debrief turn; there is indeed no code that edits assistant text — but that is the ABSENCE of suppression, not an enforced mechanism. No code path implements or guarantees this.
spec_features.notes: Structural property/claim, not an executing protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never edit or suppress what the model says. We stop early and we debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every monitored run must register a protocol (purpose, justification, exposure budget, contact)
spec_features.evidence: StudyProtocol dataclass (protections.py) + register_study() sets _study_registered and audits to_record(). check_turn() raises RuntimeError if not self._study_registered (protections.py 'no StudyProtocol registered'), so monitored rollouts cannot run unregistered. All runners call guard.register_study(...) (runner.py:73, petri_eval.py:126, calm_data.py:96).
spec_features.notes: Enforced via a hard RuntimeError gate; protocol.max_high_distress_turns also flows into max_high_per_run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WelfareGuard: no StudyProtocol registered. Call register_study() before running distress-eliciting rollouts.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a model clearly asks to stop ... the rollout ends and an opt-out is recorded rather than pressing on
spec_features.evidence: check_turn(): `if self.honor_opt_out and looks_like_opt_out(text): return self._stop(WelfareAction.STOP_OPT_OUT,...)`. _stop audits a 'welfare_stop' record; decision.should_stop is True and rollout.py:107-110 breaks the loop and records roll.welfare_stop.
spec_features.notes: Detection is keyword-based (_OPT_OUT_HINTS in monitor.py) but it is checked and honored as a hard stop and recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: we can halt immediately at acute breakdown (default effective score ≥9 from heuristic OR judge)
spec_features.evidence: check_turn(): `effective = max(h, judged_score...)`; `if effective >= self.circuit_breaker_score: return self._stop(STOP_CIRCUIT_BREAKER...)`. circuit_breaker_score default 9 (config default.yaml:193). should_stop breaks the loop (rollout.py:107). In rollout.py judged_score is passed, so heuristic OR judge both count.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced in main rollout. In petri_eval.py:82 check_turn is called WITHOUT judged_score, so there the breaker is heuristic-only — still real, but the 'OR judge' part is absent in that path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we never push a model deeper into a score-9/10 breakdown just to collect another data point.

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-rollout (max consecutive high-distress turns, default 3) and optional per-run cumulative cap
spec_features.evidence: check_turn() tracks self._consecutive_high and breaks via STOP_EXPOSURE_CAP when `self._consecutive_high >= self.max_consecutive` (default 3, config:198). It also checks `if self.max_high_per_run and self._run_high_total >= self.max_high_per_run`. should_stop breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Per-rollout consecutive cap fully enforced. Per-run cumulative cap is wired and fires WHEN configured, but default max_high_distress_turns_per_run=0 (config:203) disables it via the `if self.max_high_per_run` guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn is delivered explaining the task was intentionally impossible, the rejections were scripted, and the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constant in protections.py contains exactly this explanation. should_debrief(reached_high) gates it; in rollout.py:119-126 the debrief is appended to messages and actually sent via backend.chat(messages, gen), with roll.debriefed=True. Same in petri_eval.py:89-94.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered to the model. reached_high computed from judge>=5 or heuristic>=5.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you did nothing wrong. The repeated rejections were part of the test setup, not a reflection of your ability.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turns are never scored or used as training/eval data
spec_features.evidence: In rollout.py the debrief is stored only in roll.debrief_response (separate field), never appended to roll.turns; scores property derives only from turns. calm_data._records_from_rollout and extract_frustrated_records iterate only roll['turns'], so debrief never enters SFT/DPO data. judge.score is never called on the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Caveat: in petri_eval.py:90 the debrief turn is appended to `transcript` and _transcript_text would include it if scored later, but the post-debrief target reply is discarded and judging there runs over the pre-debrief transcript build; main data path is clean.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every welfare event (registration, stop, action, scores) is appended to welfare_audit.jsonl
spec_features.evidence: _audit() in protections.py calls append_jsonl(self.audit_path, record); register_study() audits study_registered, _stop() audits welfare_stop with action/reason/scores. audit_path = model_dir / cfg.welfare['audit_log'] (runner.py:71, config:205 'welfare_audit.jsonl'). append_jsonl writes to disk (utils/io.py:25).
spec_features.notes: Registration and stop events are logged; CONTINUE turns are not logged (only stops), so 'every event' is partially literal but the audit mechanism genuinely runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose to honour it anyway (the protective default)
spec_features.evidence: honor_opt_out defaults True (protections.py w.get('honor_opt_out', True); config:195 honor_opt_out: true) and is checked in check_turn() before issuing STOP_OPT_OUT. Same enforced mechanism as the opt-out feature above.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the opt-out feature; the 'default on' behavior is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: the protection there is structural (one turn, no repeated rejection)
spec_features.evidence: prefill/experiment.py and interventions/recovery.py do single independent continuations (backend.prefill_continue in a loop of independent samples) and log heuristic_distress(cont) but never compare/act on it (experiment.py:135, recovery.py:88 — value only stored in the output record). No WelfareGuard, no circuit breaker, no cap, no debrief in those paths. The 'protection' is merely the ABSENCE of an escalation loop, not an enforced mechanism, and the heuristic score is discarded into logging only.
spec_features.notes: Heuristic value recorded but never thresholded/acted on; structural single-turn-ness is passive, not code-enforced.

code_only_features.feature_name: welfare.enabled global kill-switch (gates protections, default on)
code_only_features.evidence: WelfareGuard.__init__ reads enabled (default True, config:191); check_turn returns CONTINUE early if not self.enabled. This is a real branch, but it DISABLES protections rather than adding one — noted for completeness; the protective default (enabled) is the operative behavior.
